title: CUET Mass Media Test 3
subject: Mass Media / Mass Communication (Code: 318)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/Mass Media - 318.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: NTA CUET (UG) Mass Media papers 2024, 2025 and 2026, analysed for format only (no questions copied)
textbooks: CBSE Mass Media Studies, Classes XI-XII (curriculum mirrored by the NTA syllabus)
Constitution of India, Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(2); Acts and Supreme Court judgments as cited
Official histories of All India Radio, Doordarshan and Indian cinema
instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
One set of 5 questions is based on a case; the set stays together.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: What radio depends on
questions.question: Radio is called a "blind" medium because it depends only on ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) sound
Why: Radio has no pictures, so it must convey everything through words, music, sound effects and silence.
Why not the others: (B) and (D) belong to TV and cinema. (C) belongs to newspapers.
Key point: Radio writers paint pictures with sound.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: Funding an event for visibility
questions.question: A bank pays for a city marathon, and its name appears on the runners' bibs and banners. This PR tool is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Sponsorship
Why: In sponsorship a company funds an event or cause in return for being seen and linked with it.
Why not the others: (B) means trying to influence lawmakers. (C) is a written statement for the media. (D) is a magazine for employees.
Key point: Sponsorship builds goodwill by linking a brand with a popular event.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: A wrongly matched newspaper term
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
options: B) Op-ed – an editorial by the editor
C) Obituary – a report on a death
D) Filler – a short item to fill space
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Op-ed – an editorial by the editor
Why: (B) is wrongly matched. The op-ed is the page "opposite the editorial", which carries opinion pieces by outside writers and columnists, not by the editor.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are correctly matched.
Key point: The editorial gives the paper's view; the op-ed gives others' views.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.sub_topic: Social and political effects of new media
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about new media:
(A) New media lets people publish without passing through traditional gatekeepers.
(B) The digital divide means the gap between print readers and TV viewers.
(C) Fake news can spread faster than its correction.
(D) New media has made editors' control over news stronger than ever.
Which of the statements given above are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B) and (D) only
Why: (B) and (D) are false. The digital divide is the gap between those who have internet access and those who do not. New media has weakened, not strengthened, editors' control, since anyone can publish.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) are correct, so (A) and (C) are wrong answers. (D) leaves out (B).
Key point: New media widens participation but brings risks such as fake news and unequal access.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: A task outside pre-production
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a pre-production task?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Colour grading the footage
Why: Colour grading adjusts the colour of recorded footage, so it belongs to post-production.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are all done before shooting begins.
Key point: Anything done to footage after it is shot is post-production.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: A film of real people and events
questions.question: A film that records real people, places and events, without a made-up story, is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Documentary
Why: A documentary deals with actual events and people, not fiction.
Why not the others: (A) tells a fictional story with actors. (B) is made from drawings or models. (C) is a fiction film built around songs.
Key point: Documentaries aim to record and explain reality.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: Departments of an advertising agency
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Department)
(A) Account servicing
(B) Creative
(C) Media
(D) Research

List-II (Work)
(I) Studies consumers and the market
(II) Writes the copy and designs the visuals
(III) Plans and buys space and airtime
(IV) Acts as the link between the client and the agency
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)
Why: Account servicing links the client and the agency (IV). The creative department makes the advertisement (II). The media department buys space and time (III), and research studies the market (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps account servicing and creative. (B) swaps creative and media. (D) swaps media and research.
Key point: An agency works through specialised departments.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: News values beyond time and place
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about news values:
(A) Impact means that an event affects a large number of people.
(B) Novelty means that an event is unusual or unexpected.
(C) Conflict covers disputes, clashes and contests.
(D) Proximity means that an event involves famous people.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. A price rise has impact, a man biting a dog has novelty, and a strike or an election has conflict.
Why not the others: (D) is false. Proximity means nearness to the reader; events involving famous people have prominence. Options (B) and (D) include (D), and (C) leaves out (B).
Key point: The more news values an event has, the bigger the story.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: Press laws in order of time
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
(A) The Indian Press Act
(B) The Right to Information Act
(C) The Press and Registration of Books Act
(D) The setting up of the first Press Council of India
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (A), (D), (B)
Why: The Press and Registration of Books Act was passed in 1867, and the Indian Press Act in 1910. The first Press Council was set up in 1966, and the RTI Act came in 2005.
Why not the others: (A) puts 1966 before 1910. (B) puts 1910 before 1867. (D) puts 2005 before 1966.
Key point: Press laws moved from colonial control to rights for citizens.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.sub_topic: Types of social media platforms
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Facebook is a microblogging site limited to short text posts.
(B) LinkedIn is a professional networking site.
(C) WordPress is a blogging platform.
(D) Pinterest is used mainly to share and save images.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (B), (C) and (D) only
Why: (B), (C) and (D) are correct. LinkedIn is for careers, WordPress hosts blogs, and Pinterest is built around images.
Why not the others: (A) is false. Facebook is a social networking site that carries long posts, photos and videos. Options (B) and (D) include (A), and (C) leaves out (C).
Key point: Platforms are grouped by the kind of content and connection they offer.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: Levels of communication and examples
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Level)
(A) Intrapersonal
(B) Interpersonal
(C) Group
(D) Mass

List-II (Example)
(I) A panchayat meeting of twenty villagers
(II) A news bulletin on a national TV channel
(III) A student rehearsing a speech in her mind
(IV) Two friends talking on the phone
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Intrapersonal communication happens within one mind (III). Interpersonal is between two people (IV). Group communication is within a small gathering (I), and mass communication reaches a vast audience through a medium (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps intrapersonal and interpersonal. (C) swaps interpersonal and group. (D) swaps group and mass.
Key point: The levels differ in the number of people and the use of a medium.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: Reporting that digs out hidden wrongdoing
questions.question: Reporting that spends weeks or months uncovering corruption or wrongdoing that people in power want to hide is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Investigative journalism
Why: Investigative journalism uses long research, documents and sources to expose hidden wrongdoing.
Why not the others: (B) reports on development issues. (C) is reporting by ordinary people. (D) covers fashion, food and travel.
Key point: Investigative reporting is the press acting as a watchdog.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: An advertisement written like a news article
questions.question: A paid advertisement that is designed to look like a news article or feature is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) An advertorial
Why: An advertorial (advertisement + editorial) is paid content made to look like editorial matter. Ethical papers label it clearly.
Why not the others: (B) is the paper's own opinion. (C) is an opinion piece by an outside writer. (D) is a regular piece by one writer.
Key point: Readers must be able to tell paid content from news.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: How a brand is seen
questions.question: The picture of a brand that exists in consumers' minds, built from advertising, use and word of mouth, is called its:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Brand image
Why: Brand image is how consumers see a brand: the feelings and ideas they link with it.
Why not the others: (B) is a legally registered name or symbol. (C) is the price at which a product sells. (D) is a brand's share of total sales.
Key point: Advertising and PR work together to build brand image.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: India's first campus community radio
questions.question: India's first campus community radio station, started at Anna University, Chennai, in 2004, is ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Anna FM
Why: Anna FM went on air on 1 February 2004 as India's first campus community radio station.
Why not the others: (A) is a commercial FM channel. (B) is AIR's entertainment service, started in 1957. (D) was an educational FM service of IGNOU.
Key point: Community radio is run by and for a local community.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: Steps in making a radio programme
questions.question:
Arrange the following steps of making a recorded radio programme in the correct order:
(A) Editing the recording
(B) Broadcasting the programme
(C) Writing the script
(D) Recording in the studio
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (C), (D), (A), (B)
Why: The script is written first, then recorded in the studio. The recording is edited, and only then broadcast.
Why not the others: (A) records before there is a script. (C) edits before recording. (D) broadcasts before editing.
Key point: Recorded programmes allow mistakes to be removed before broadcast.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.sub_topic: The meaning of the letters OTT
questions.question: OTT platforms such as streaming services get their name from the phrase:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Over the top
Why: OTT means "over the top": the content is delivered over the internet, going past cable and broadcast networks.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are not what the letters stand for.
Key point: OTT is one of the fastest-growing new media trends.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.sub_topic: Online crimes and what they mean
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Crime)
(A) Hacking
(B) Online fraud
(C) Morphing
(D) Ransomware

List-II (Meaning)
(I) Altering a person's photo to shame or defame them
(II) Locking a victim's files until money is paid
(III) Cheating people out of money over the internet
(IV) Breaking into a computer system without permission
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Hacking is breaking in without permission (IV). Online fraud cheats people of money (III). Morphing alters photos to defame (I), and ransomware locks files for money (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps hacking and fraud. (B) swaps fraud and morphing. (D) swaps morphing and ransomware.
Key point: All of these are offences under the IT Act, 2000.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: Advertising a company rather than a product
questions.question: An oil company runs advertisements about its tree-planting work, without mentioning any of its products. This is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Institutional advertising
Why: Institutional (corporate) advertising builds goodwill for the company as a whole, not for one product.
Why not the others: (A) promotes a product. (B) compares brands. (D) is small advertisements grouped by category.
Key point: Institutional advertising works on reputation, much like PR.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: A reporter's fixed area of coverage
questions.question: A reporter who regularly covers one area, such as the police, courts or education, is said to cover a ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) beat
Why: A beat is the area or subject a reporter covers regularly, building sources and knowledge over time.
Why not the others: (A) is a regular opinion piece. (C) is a news agency service. (D) is a place in a page or schedule.
Key point: Beat reporters become experts in their field.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: Camera angles and their effect
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Angle)
(A) High angle
(B) Low angle
(C) Bird's-eye view
(D) Dutch angle

List-II (Effect)
(I) The subject looks small or weak
(II) The scene is seen from directly overhead
(III) The frame is tilted to create unease
(IV) The subject looks powerful
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(I), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)
Why: A camera looking down (high angle) makes a subject look weak (I), and one looking up (low angle) makes it look powerful (IV). A bird's-eye view is from directly overhead (II), and a Dutch angle tilts the frame (III).
Why not the others: (B) swaps high and low angle. (C) swaps low angle and bird's-eye view. (D) swaps bird's-eye and Dutch angle.
Key point: Camera angle shapes how the viewer feels about a subject.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.sub_topic: One device doing many jobs
questions.question: A smartphone that works as a phone, camera, radio, TV and newspaper is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Technological convergence
Why: Technological convergence is the coming together of different media functions in one device or platform.
Why not the others: (A) is one company owning many media. (B) is the blending of cultures. (C) is a company buying rivals in the same line of business.
Key point: Digital technology lets every medium share one platform.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.sub_topic: Content that spreads very fast
questions.question: A video that is shared by millions of people within a few hours is said to have:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Gone viral
Why: Content goes viral when people share it so fast and widely that it spreads like a virus.
Why not the others: (A) is not a term used. (C) means stored away. (D) means checked by moderators.
Key point: Viral spread can carry both useful information and fake news.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: A drama that runs on and on
questions.question: A TV drama that runs in regular episodes over months or years, following the lives of the same families, is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Soap opera
Why: A soap opera is a continuing serial with ongoing storylines and the same characters.
Why not the others: (A) dramatises real events. (C) is a comedy with self-contained episodes. (D) is a single film made for TV.
Key point: The name comes from American radio serials once sponsored by soap makers.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: Indian films from 1937 to 1975 in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following films in the order of their release:
(A) Kisan Kanya, an early Indian colour film
(B) Sholay
(C) Do Bigha Zamin
(D) Mother India
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (C), (D), (B)
Why: Kisan Kanya, made in colour in India, came out in 1937. Bimal Roy's Do Bigha Zamin followed in 1953 and Mother India in 1957. Sholay was released in 1975.
Why not the others: (B) puts 1953 before 1937. (C) puts 1957 before 1953. (D) puts Sholay before Mother India.
Key point: Mother India was India's first film nominated for the Oscar for best foreign-language film.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: A large roadside advertising board
questions.question: A large advertising board put up beside a road or on a building is called a ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) billboard
Why: A billboard (hoarding) is a large outdoor board placed where many people pass.
Why not the others: (A) and (D) are online formats. (C) is a printed sheet handed out.
Key point: Outdoor advertising reaches people on the move.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: A release that may not be published early
questions.question: A press release marked "Not for publication before 6 p.m. on 15 August" carries:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) An embargo
Why: An embargo is a request that news not be published before a stated time.
Why not the others: (A) gives the place and date of filing. (B) is a statement that limits responsibility. (C) names the writer.
Key point: Journalists respect embargoes so that sources keep trusting them.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: Harming a reputation with false statements
questions.question: Publishing a false statement that damages a person's reputation is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Defamation
Why: Defamation is a false statement, spoken or published, that lowers a person's reputation in the eyes of others.
Why not the others: (A) concerns acts against the state. (B) is copying another's work. (D) concerns disrespect to courts.
Key point: Truth published for the public good is a defence against defamation.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.sub_topic: What new media does not have
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of new media?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) A fixed one-way flow
Why: New media is interactive: users can reply, share and create. A fixed one-way flow belongs to the traditional mass media.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are all features of new media.
Key point: In new media, the audience can also be the sender.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: Culture spread by the mass media
questions.question: Film songs, cricket, TV serials and fashion trends that are enjoyed by large numbers of people and spread through the mass media are examples of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Popular culture
Why: Popular culture is the culture of ordinary people in large numbers, spread and shaped by the mass media.
Why not the others: (A) is passed down within a local community. (B) is the culture of a small, educated or wealthy group. (C) means objects and tools made by a society.
Key point: The mass media both spread popular culture and profit from it.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: The one claim that sets a product apart
questions.question: The single benefit that an advertisement stresses to set a product apart from its rivals is called its:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) USP
Why: The USP (unique selling proposition) is the special benefit that only this product claims to offer.
Why not the others: (A) is a catchy line, which may express the USP but is not the same thing. (B) is a symbol. (C) is a short song.
Key point: A strong USP gives buyers a reason to choose one product.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.sub_topic: The trail people leave online
questions.question: The record of a person's posts, searches, likes and comments that stays online is called their:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Digital footprint
Why: A digital footprint is the trail of data a person leaves online, which others may see long after.
Why not the others: (A) is the gap in internet access. (B) is a mobile internet package. (C) is an electronic way of signing documents.
Key point: Thinking before posting protects one's digital footprint.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: Film crew and their jobs
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Crew member)
(A) Cinematographer
(B) Editor
(C) Art director
(D) Choreographer

List-II (Job)
(I) Designs the dance movements
(II) Plans the camera work and lighting
(III) Joins the shots into a sequence
(IV) Designs the sets and the look of the locations
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
Why: The cinematographer is in charge of camera and light (II). The editor assembles the shots (III). The art director designs the sets (IV), and the choreographer designs dances (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps cinematographer and editor. (C) swaps editor and art director. (D) swaps art director and choreographer.
Key point: A film is the work of many specialists led by the director.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: Media laws and what they deal with
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Law)
(A) Contempt of Courts Act, 1971
(B) Copyright Act, 1957
(C) Working Journalists Act, 1955
(D) Prasar Bharati Act, 1990

List-II (Subject)
(I) Protecting the rights of authors and creators
(II) Punishing acts that lower the authority of courts
(III) Setting up an autonomous body for AIR and Doordarshan
(IV) Service conditions and wages of newspaper staff
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
Why: The Contempt of Courts Act protects the authority of courts (II). The Copyright Act protects creators (I). The Working Journalists Act covers newspaper staff's service conditions (IV), and the Prasar Bharati Act set up an autonomous broadcaster (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps copyright and working journalists. (B) swaps contempt and copyright. (C) swaps working journalists and Prasar Bharati.
Key point: Media laws protect courts, creators, workers and the public.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: Roles and tools in a TV studio
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about television production:
(A) The producer is in charge of the budget, the schedule and the project as a whole.
(B) The vision mixer switches between camera feeds in the control room.
(C) The lighting director operates the cameras during the shoot.
(D) A teleprompter shows the script to the presenter in front of the camera lens.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. The producer runs the project, the vision mixer cuts between cameras, and the teleprompter lets the presenter read while looking at the lens.
Why not the others: (C) is false. The lighting director plans and sets the lights; camera operators run the cameras. Options (B) and (C) include (C), and (A) leaves out (D).
Key point: A TV crew is a team of specialists, each with one job.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: Doordarshan serials in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following Doordarshan serials in the order in which they were first telecast:
(A) Buniyaad
(B) Mahabharat
(C) Hum Log
(D) Ramayan
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (C), (A), (D), (B)
Why: Hum Log began in 1984 and Buniyaad in 1986. Ramayan followed in 1987, and Mahabharat in 1988.
Why not the others: (B) puts Buniyaad before Hum Log. (C) puts Ramayan before Buniyaad. (D) puts Mahabharat before Ramayan.
Key point: These serials drew huge audiences and made television a national habit in the 1980s.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: Radio terms and their meanings
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Jingle
(B) Signature tune
(C) Cue
(D) Fade-in

List-II (Meaning)
(I) The tune that opens a particular programme
(II) A signal to begin speaking or playing
(III) A short, catchy musical piece, often for a station or advertisement
(IV) Raising the sound gradually from silence
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)
Why: A jingle is a short catchy tune (III). A signature tune opens a programme (I). A cue signals someone to start (II), and a fade-in raises the sound gradually (IV).
Why not the others: (A) swaps jingle and signature tune. (B) swaps signature tune and cue. (C) swaps cue and fade-in.
Key point: Music and sound cues give radio programmes their identity and flow.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.sub_topic: Accounts that post automatically
questions.question: Fake social media accounts run by software to post and share content automatically are called ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) bots
Why: Bots are automated accounts. They are often used to make a message look more popular than it is.
Why not the others: (A) are people who post to provoke. (B) check content. (C) are real people with large followings.
Key point: Bots can spread fake news and distort public opinion.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: The written form of a film
questions.question: The written version of a film, with its scenes, dialogue and action described shot by shot, is called the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Screenplay
Why: The screenplay sets out every scene with its dialogue and directions.
Why not the others: (A) is a short summary of the story. (B) is a preview to promote a film. (D) tells the crew and cast when to report each day.
Key point: The screenplay is the blueprint of a film.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: What AM stands for and how it travels
questions.question: Which statement about AM radio is correct?
options: A) It varies the frequency and has a short range
B) It is used only by community radio stations
C) It varies the amplitude and can travel far
D) It gives better sound quality than FM
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) It varies the amplitude and can travel far
Why: AM (amplitude modulation) varies the strength of the carrier wave. Medium and short-wave AM signals can cover long distances.
Why not the others: (A) describes FM. (B) is wrong, since community radio in India uses FM. (D) is wrong, as FM sounds clearer.
Key point: AM reaches farther; FM sounds better.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: A small microphone worn on clothing
questions.question: A small microphone clipped to a presenter's collar, leaving the hands free, is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Lapel microphone
Why: A lapel (lavalier) microphone is tiny and clipped to clothing near the mouth.
Why not the others: (A) is held over the speaker on a pole. (B) is a long, highly directional microphone. (C) is a delicate studio microphone.
Key point: Lapel microphones suit interviews and talk shows.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: Facts about public relations
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about public relations:
(A) Edward Bernays wrote Crystallizing Public Opinion (1923).
(B) The Public Relations Society of India was founded in 1958.
(C) National Public Relations Day is observed in India on 21 April.
(D) A press conference is a written statement mailed to journalists.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (D) only
Why: Only (D) is false. A press conference is a meeting at which journalists put questions to a speaker; a written statement sent out is a press release.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Options (A), (C) and (D) name a correct statement as false.
Key point: The press conference is two-way; the press release is one-way.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: Replacing a coloured background
questions.question: A weather presenter stands in front of a plain green wall, and a map is shown behind her on screen. The technique used is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Chroma key
Why: Chroma key removes one colour (usually green or blue) from the picture and replaces it with another image.
Why not the others: (A) lays one image faintly over another. (C) shows two pictures side by side. (D) stops the picture on one frame.
Key point: The presenter must not wear the key colour, or parts of them vanish.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: A short film to promote a coming release
questions.question: A short preview made from scenes of a film and shown before its release to attract audiences is called a ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) trailer
Why: A trailer is a short promotional preview made from a film's scenes.
Why not the others: (B) is a printed poster. (C) is an early edit of the film. (D) is a single photograph from the film.
Key point: Trailers are part of a film's publicity and distribution.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: Genres and their features
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about film genres:
(A) Science fiction builds stories on imagined science or the future.
(B) Raja Harishchandra (1913) was a mythological film.
(C) Melodrama keeps emotions low and avoids music.
(D) War films show soldiers and battles, real or imagined.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. Science fiction imagines new science, Raja Harishchandra retold a story from mythology, and war films centre on war.
Why not the others: (C) is false. Melodrama heightens emotion, often with music, to move the audience. Options (B) and (D) include (C), and (A) leaves out (D).
Key point: Genres are recognised by their typical stories and styles.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: Why the van's announcement was lost
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

Before the monsoon, the district health officer, Dr Meena, wants villagers in Kolar block to prevent dengue. She sends an SMS in English to every registered phone: "Eliminate stagnant water to prevent vector-borne disease." She also hires a van that drives through the villages playing a recorded announcement. The van passes during the village fair, when loudspeakers are playing film songs.

Three weeks later, dengue cases are rising. No one has called the helpline number in the SMS, and the health office has no idea how people understood the message.

Dr Meena changes her plan. ASHA workers, who live in the villages, meet women's self-help groups and speak in the local language. They show pictures of a water tank, a flower pot and an old tyre holding water, and ask the women where such water collects in their own homes. When the women say that covering tanks is hard, the workers show them how to use a cloth. Within a month, the number of new cases falls.

Question: The film songs playing at the fair, which drowned out the van's announcement, are an example of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Noise
Why: Noise is anything that interferes with a message between the sender and the receiver. Here loud music made the announcement hard to hear.
Why not the others: (B) is the receiver's response to the sender. (C) is the medium that carries the message, here the van's loudspeaker. (D) is putting an idea into words or symbols.
Key point: Noise can be physical, like music, or semantic, like unfamiliar words.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: Where the SMS went wrong
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

Before the monsoon, the district health officer, Dr Meena, wants villagers in Kolar block to prevent dengue. She sends an SMS in English to every registered phone: "Eliminate stagnant water to prevent vector-borne disease." She also hires a van that drives through the villages playing a recorded announcement. The van passes during the village fair, when loudspeakers are playing film songs.

Three weeks later, dengue cases are rising. No one has called the helpline number in the SMS, and the health office has no idea how people understood the message.

Dr Meena changes her plan. ASHA workers, who live in the villages, meet women's self-help groups and speak in the local language. They show pictures of a water tank, a flower pot and an old tyre holding water, and ask the women where such water collects in their own homes. When the women say that covering tanks is hard, the workers show them how to use a cloth. Within a month, the number of new cases falls.

Question: The SMS failed mainly because Dr Meena put her idea into words that the villagers could not easily understand. This is a failure at the stage of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Encoding
Why: Encoding is turning an idea into a code the receiver shares. English technical words like "vector-borne" did not match the villagers' code, so they could not decode the message.
Why not the others: (A) worked, since the SMS reached the phones. (B) is the response, which came later or not at all. (D) is an editor's selection of news.
Key point: A message is only understood when sender and receiver share a code.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: The shape of the first plan
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

Before the monsoon, the district health officer, Dr Meena, wants villagers in Kolar block to prevent dengue. She sends an SMS in English to every registered phone: "Eliminate stagnant water to prevent vector-borne disease." She also hires a van that drives through the villages playing a recorded announcement. The van passes during the village fair, when loudspeakers are playing film songs.

Three weeks later, dengue cases are rising. No one has called the helpline number in the SMS, and the health office has no idea how people understood the message.

Dr Meena changes her plan. ASHA workers, who live in the villages, meet women's self-help groups and speak in the local language. They show pictures of a water tank, a flower pot and an old tyre holding water, and ask the women where such water collects in their own homes. When the women say that covering tanks is hard, the workers show them how to use a cloth. Within a month, the number of new cases falls.

Question: Dr Meena's first plan, with messages sent out and no way of hearing back, is closest to which kind of model?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A linear model
Why: A linear model shows communication as a one-way flow from sender to receiver, with no feedback. The SMS and the van spoke to people but could not hear them.
Why not the others: (A) and (D) show a two-way exchange in which both sides send and receive. (C) shows communication growing like a spiral over time.
Key point: Linear models leave out feedback, which is why they explain failures like this one.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: Why the ASHA workers were understood
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

Before the monsoon, the district health officer, Dr Meena, wants villagers in Kolar block to prevent dengue. She sends an SMS in English to every registered phone: "Eliminate stagnant water to prevent vector-borne disease." She also hires a van that drives through the villages playing a recorded announcement. The van passes during the village fair, when loudspeakers are playing film songs.

Three weeks later, dengue cases are rising. No one has called the helpline number in the SMS, and the health office has no idea how people understood the message.

Dr Meena changes her plan. ASHA workers, who live in the villages, meet women's self-help groups and speak in the local language. They show pictures of a water tank, a flower pot and an old tyre holding water, and ask the women where such water collects in their own homes. When the women say that covering tanks is hard, the workers show them how to use a cloth. Within a month, the number of new cases falls.

Question: The ASHA workers live in the villages and share the women's language and daily life. In Wilbur Schramm's terms, their message worked because there was a large overlap in the two sides':
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Fields of experience
Why: Schramm said that communication succeeds when the sender's and receiver's fields of experience (language, culture, knowledge) overlap. The ASHA workers and the women share much of this.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are parts of the process but are not Schramm's explanation here. (C) has nothing to do with a face-to-face meeting.
Key point: The more experience sender and receiver share, the easier it is to understand each other.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: What changed in the second plan
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

Before the monsoon, the district health officer, Dr Meena, wants villagers in Kolar block to prevent dengue. She sends an SMS in English to every registered phone: "Eliminate stagnant water to prevent vector-borne disease." She also hires a van that drives through the villages playing a recorded announcement. The van passes during the village fair, when loudspeakers are playing film songs.

Three weeks later, dengue cases are rising. No one has called the helpline number in the SMS, and the health office has no idea how people understood the message.

Dr Meena changes her plan. ASHA workers, who live in the villages, meet women's self-help groups and speak in the local language. They show pictures of a water tank, a flower pot and an old tyre holding water, and ask the women where such water collects in their own homes. When the women say that covering tanks is hard, the workers show them how to use a cloth. Within a month, the number of new cases falls.

Question: Which statement best explains why Dr Meena's second plan succeeded?
options: A) It reached more people than the SMS could reach
B) It used a more modern medium than the van
C) It let the workers hear back and adjust the message
D) It repeated the same message more often than before
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) It let the workers hear back and adjust the message
Why: The ASHA workers asked questions, heard the women's difficulty with covering tanks, and adjusted their advice. Feedback made the communication two-way.
Why not the others: (A) is not stated, since the SMS went to every phone. (B) is wrong, as face-to-face talk is not a modern medium. (D) is wrong, because the message itself changed.
Key point: Two-way communication lets the sender correct a message until it is understood.
